In this problem, we know this is a hypothesis test because we are
asked to “test the claim at the 0.05 significance level.” We are told
that Americans spent an average (or a mean) of $276 per month.
Also, the data that is provided is quantitative (numerical). These
factors all tell us that we are going to conduct a hypothesis test for
a population mean. Paraphrasing, we wish to test the claim that the
mean amount that consumers are spending on impulse purchases
: We are testing 2022 data against the mean from 2021. So, the null hypothesis is that there is
no change, and Americans continue to spend $276 on average per month on impulse
purchases. The alternative hypothesis is that they are spending more.
, this is a right tailed test.
